To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the variability in device parameters can be separated into the sampling level contributions of differences between lots, differences between wafers within a lot, and differences between contact windows within a wafer, 2) the processing components of contact window patterning can also be identified as contributors to variability, 3) the relative contribution to variability made by each processing step and sampling level can be determined, 4) the relative contribution made by each processing component can be identified at each sampling level and

the variability of the parameter of interest can be broken down into contributions due to the sampling levels and the process steps, and that the contributions due to the process steps can be broken down by the sampling levels.

the variance of a process parameter can be partitioned into components representing variability at different sampling levels, and that the variance component analysis can be used to identify the sources of variability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of statistical methods to the analysis of data obtained during the manufacturing of integrated circuit devices.
the application of statistical techniques to problems in semiconductor technology.
the application of statistical techniques to the analysis of parameter variability in integrated circuits, and the identification of sources of variability in the manufacturing process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the statistical techniques described in this paper provide a powerful set of tools to aid in the understanding of parameter variability and its sources.
statistical sampling and variance component estimation can be effectively used to separate the variability of integrated circuit device parameters into its component parts.
the variance component technique provides a powerful and flexible method for analyzing the variability of a process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the techniques of statistical sampling and variance component estimation provide the means for identifying the sources of variability in integrated circuits device parameters and, in addition, for identifying the sources that are responsible for the greatest portion of the total variability.
the techniques described in this paper provide a means for separating variability in integrated circuits device parameters into the sampling level and manufacturing process components.
the techniques described are useful in the identification of the sources of variability for integrated circuit parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
statistical methods can be used to analyze variability in the patterning process.
the variance component analysis is a useful tool in the semiconductor industry for identifying and controlling variability in manufacturing processes.

the statistical methods used can be applied to any parameter of the manufacturing process, and that they can help in the identification of the sources of variability in that process, and thus help in the identification and correction of the sources of that variability.
